questions.text: Do you live in a house or a flat?

cueCard.explain: and explain why you admire this person.

questions.text: Describe an older person you admire.
questions.say: Thank you. Now, in Part 2, I'm going to give you a topic, and I'd like you to talk about it for one to two minutes. Before you talk, you'll have one minute to think about what you're going to say. You can make some notes if you wish. Here is your topic. Describe an older person you admire. You should say: who this person is; how you know them; what they are like; and explain why you admire this person.

questions.text: Do you think you will be like this person when you are older?
questions.say: Thank you. Do you think you will be like this person when you are older?

questions.text: What can older people teach younger people?
questions.say: Thank you. We've been talking about an older person you admire, and I'd like to discuss with you some more general questions related to this. Let's consider first of all old age. What can older people teach younger people?

questions.text: Do older people in your country usually live with their families?
questions.say: Do older people in your country usually live with their families?

questions.text: What are the advantages of working after the normal age of retirement?
questions.say: What are the advantages of working after the normal age of retirement?

questions.text: Why do young people and older people sometimes disagree?
questions.say: Now let's talk about generations. Why do young people and older people sometimes disagree?

questions.text: How is life for young people today different from life for their grandparents?
questions.say: How is life for young people today different from life for their grandparents?

questions.text: What could be done to help different generations understand each other better?
